evidence: src/application/OrderDto.ts defines toOrderDto. AdvanceOrderUseCase, CancelOrderUseCase, GetOrderUseCase, ListOrdersByStateUseCase and PlaceOrderUseCase all use it, so order output mapping lives in one place.
src/application/PlaceOrderUseCase.ts uses OrderLineDto as input and builds lines with the domain's createOrderLine and Order.place, so line validation stays in the domain.
src/application/ListOrdersByStateUseCase.ts checks the state with the domain's isOrderState instead of keeping its own list of states.
src/application/AdvanceOrderUseCase.ts calls order.advanceTo(target) and leaves the transition rules to the domain. It is the only place that calls stock.dispatch.
src/application/CancelOrderUseCase.ts calls order.cancel() and then stock.release; src/application/PlaceOrderUseCase.ts calls stock.reserve. Each stock effect happens in one place.

AdvanceOrderUseCase, CancelOrderUseCase and GetOrderUseCase repeat the same guard: findById, then throw DomainError('not_found', `Order ${orderId} does not exist`). This is minor boilerplate, not a duplicated business rule.
src/application/GetStockLevelsUseCase.ts builds StockLevelDto inline from ProductRepository.findAll(). The module has no shared stock-level mapper that this skips.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The src/application module is one coherent layer of use cases for order fulfilment and stock queries. Each use case is a thin coordinator: it calls domain repositories and services and returns DTOs. The domain owns the business rules. Order handles state changes through Order.place, advanceTo and cancel. OrderLine validates lines through createOrderLine. OrderState validates states through isOrderState. The module's own abstractions are used consistently. Every order use case maps its result through the shared toOrderDto in OrderDto.ts. PlaceOrderUseCase reuses OrderLineDto as its input type. ID creation goes through the IdGenerator port. GetStockLevelsUseCase builds StockLevelDto inline. That is a small style difference, not a bypass, because no stock-level mapper exists to bypass. Three use cases repeat the same find-or-throw guard (DomainError "not_found"). This is small repeated boilerplate rather than a business rule spread across files. Moving it into a helper would be a nice cleanup, but it does not justify a fail. Each stock side effect lives in exactly one place: reserve on place, release on cancel, dispatch on ship.
